paragraphs.text: Patient reports no plans to harm themselves and no access to firearms or other lethal means.

The patient reports experiencing a major depressive episode for the past three months, since losing their job in July. They describe persistent feelings of sadness, crying almost every day, and a loss of interest in activities they previously enjoyed. The patient also reports difficulty with sleep, waking up at 4 AM and being unable to return to sleep, resulting in approximately five hours of sleep per night. They mention a poor appetite and a ten-pound weight loss. The patient denies any thoughts of self-harm or suicide, stating that while they sometimes wish they would not wake up, they do not have any plans or intentions to harm themselves.

The provider discusses a family history of depression and alcoholism, noting that the patient has never been hospitalized for psychiatric reasons but has seen a therapist once in college. The patient denies any current use of alcohol or other drugs, and is currently taking lisinopril for blood pressure. The patient has no known allergies.

The provider proposes a treatment plan of sertraline, 50 milligrams daily, to address the major depressive episode. The provider will see the patient again in two weeks and will not prescribe a sleeping pill or benzodiazepine at this time. Side effects such as nausea and headache are discussed, and the alternative of therapy alone is also considered. The patient agrees to try the sertraline.
